All — quick legal take and proposed compromise language below. I'll highlight commercial exposures so Marissa can weigh tradeoffs.

Summary of risk: Consolidation itself is fine; the real cost driver is their choice of "post-billing" as the measurement point. If we measure guardband post-billing when pro-ration and proration credits are applied, we could understate their committed baseline and trigger fewer true-ups — favorable to Novus. Conversely, their burst carveout (250%) is material: if we accept an absolute hard-floor for bursts, we may have to fund significant credits during onboarding months.

Proposed approach:
1) Accept consolidation language but require the calculation to be anchored to "invoiceable usage before credits and pro-rata adjustments" (i.e., pre-billing credits). That preserves our baseline math.
2) Offer a capped burst carveout: allow a one-off "burst credit" for months >250% of monthly commit, capped at the lesser of 30% of burst overage or $X (commercial number to be filled).
3) Add explicit anti-double-count: "Credits previously applied to resolve a pricing discrepancy shall be deducted from any guardband calculus for the subsequent 12 months."

Draft clause (suggested redline text):
"The consolidated guardband calculation shall be performed on invoiceable usage prior to application of any customer-specific credits, discounts, or pro‑rata adjustments. For months in which usage exceeds 250% of the monthly commit, Redwood will allow a one-time burst credit equal to the lesser of (a) 30% of the amount by which usage exceeded the monthly commit, or (b) $[COMMERCIAL_CAP]. Previously issued credits will be reconciled and excluded from guardband computations for a 12‑month period following issuance."

Operational note for Laura: if billing cannot produce pre-credit invoiceable numbers easily, we can add a clean-up clause allowing a 30 day post-invoice reconciliation window.

Marissa — commercial choices: if we include a capped burst concession, I recommend we: (a) require a 12-month minimum committed baseline; (b) tie the cap $[COMMERCIAL_CAP] to a small percentage of ARR so we don't over-index.

I can convert the draft into track-changes if this direction is acceptable.

— Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
